title: Keep visible price and availability accurate
statement: The price, currency, and stock state shown on a product page reflect what the checkout will charge and whether the item can be bought, and no figure is emitted for a product whose real state the system does not know.
rationale: A page promising a price the checkout does not honour costs the buyer their time and the merchant their credibility, and stale stock state converts a purchase attempt into a failure at the last step.
implementation: Read price and stock from the system of record at render time, or revalidate them at checkout and surface the discrepancy. Where a value is unavailable, omit it rather than rendering a placeholder.

verification.method: Sample product routes and compare the rendered price, currency, and stock state against the values the ordering system returns for the same item.

caution: The cited documentation requires that price and availability match the landing page. This record never writes a commercial value automatically, because a wrong price is a transaction the merchant may be bound by.

title: Declare product identifiers only where they genuinely exist
statement: A trade identifier, manufacturer part number, or brand is emitted only when the catalogue holds the real value for that item, and no value is synthesised from the product name, the internal key, or a pattern.
rationale: These identifiers are used to match an item against other listings of the same item, so a fabricated value attaches the product to something it is not.
implementation: Emit each identifier field from a catalogue column that holds it, and leave the field absent when that column is empty. Report items missing identifiers as a catalogue gap rather than filling them.

verification.method: Compare emitted identifier values against the catalogue record for the same item and report any value present in the markup but absent from the catalogue.

caution: Inventing an identifier is the single most damaging fabrication available in this domain, because it silently merges one merchant's product with another's. That is why no automatic path exists to write one.

title: Give each purchasable variant its own canonical address
statement: Where variants differ in price, availability, or identifier, each is reachable at its own address that canonicalises to itself, rather than existing only as a selection made by script on a shared address.
rationale: A variant that exists only after a selection has no address to link to, cite, or list, so its distinct price and stock state cannot be represented anywhere outside the page.
implementation: Give the variant a path or a stable parameter the server renders from, and canonicalise it to itself. Where variants differ only cosmetically, keep one address and represent the choice on the page.

verification.method: Request each variant address directly and confirm the server renders that variant's price and stock state, and that the canonical value names the variant rather than the parent.

caution: Splitting variants across addresses multiplies the crawlable surface, so it is warranted where the variants genuinely differ commercially and harmful where they do not. Confidence is medium because the threshold is a catalogue judgement rather than a documented rule.

title: Keep discontinued products at a resolvable address
statement: A product that will not return is handled by a deliberate rule: a permanent redirect to a genuine replacement, or a removed status with a page that explains the removal and offers the category, rather than a soft landing that reports success.
rationale: Catalogues churn continuously, so the handling of a withdrawn product is a recurring path rather than an exception, and an unspecified rule produces an empty page returning success every time.
implementation: Redirect only where a specific replacement exists, and otherwise return the removed status with a useful page. Never redirect a withdrawn product to the home page, which tells the visitor nothing about what happened.

verification.method: Request a sample of withdrawn product addresses and record the status, the redirect target where present, and whether the target is a specific replacement or a generic destination.

caution: This record covers the catalogue-specific choice between replacement and removal. The general requirement that a removed resource must not answer with success is stated separately and is a prerequisite here.

title: State shipping and return terms where the offer appears
statement: The delivery cost, delivery window, and return window that apply to an item are stated on the page that offers it, and any machine-readable copy of those terms matches the visible text.
rationale: A buyer decides on the total cost and the risk of returning the item, so terms held only in a separate policy page leave the decision being made on incomplete information.
implementation: Render the terms from the same configuration the checkout applies, and where terms vary by destination say which destination the stated terms assume.

verification.method: Compare the delivery and return terms rendered on product routes against the terms the checkout applies for the same item and destination.

caution: Delivery and return terms may carry legal weight in the buyer's jurisdiction, so they are never generated or inferred here. Where the terms cannot be read from configuration, the gap is reported for a human to fill.

title: Treat merchant surface verification as a manual action
statement: Claiming a merchant account, verifying ownership of the store, and resolving listing disapprovals are recorded as actions requiring a person with account access, and are never reported as work this process can complete.
rationale: These steps happen inside an operator's console behind an authenticated session that no audit holds, so listing them as automatable misrepresents what the audit can deliver.
implementation: Produce the prerequisite list the person will need, note what evidence to capture from the console afterwards, and stop. Do not attach an expected outcome to the submission.

verification.method: Confirm each merchant-console item in the report is marked as requiring account access and carries no claimed completion by the audit.

caution: This describes the boundary of what an automated audit can do rather than a property of the web, so it carries no external citation. Console workflows change often, which is why the record fixes the boundary rather than the steps.
